This file is deliberately absent from frontx-template.json's ownershipBoundaries, so `frontx add` never copies it into a seeded project and this template claims ownership of no root package.json anywhere. The MFE packages below pin their @gears-frontx dependencies to exact published versions, which is what a seeded project installs. Inside this monorepo those pins would fetch registry tarballs instead of resolving to local source, so the overrides here redirect the pinned names a developer edits to their local source instead. @gears-frontx/ui-kit is deliberately NOT among them: it is a published component library an MFE consumes, not a layer the MFE is developed against, so leaving it on its exact pin means the scaffold resolves in this monorepo exactly what a seeded project resolves — the whole point of depending on the kit rather than vendoring it. The cost is that edits to packages/ui-kit are invisible here; the kit is developed and demoed from its own workspace (`npm run demo:ui-kit`) and reaches an MFE through a publish, so exercise a kit change there and re-pin once it ships. Because they redirect rather than re-declare, the installed versions still satisfy the pins and `npm ls` stays clean. This makes local edits to template-shell/packages/* (react, auth, framework, i18n, state) and to packages/api, packages/gts-plugin, packages/mfes visible for MFEs' own direct imports of those names — it does NOT reach edits to the latter three through frontx-template-shell's own pre-built dist-lib/build/mf-gts, since template-shell's own package.json pins gts-plugin/mfes/api to their published versions with no override of its own; that bundle only picks up local edits after template-shell itself is rebuilt. Bootstrap order matters: `npm install` here is NOT sufficient by itself — the whole stack below this one must be built first: this repo's ecosystem packages (`npm ci && npm run build:packages` at the root), then template-shell as a whole (`npm run build`, which sequences its publishable package before its subpackages — they type-check against the declarations it emits, so the reverse order fails on @gears-frontx/framework). Call template-shell's own `build` rather than its `build:package`/`build:packages` by hand; those two are order-sensitive. See this package's README for the exact sequence. Keep this file free of version numbers: every entry below is a path or a glob, so the pins remain the single place a version is written down.
